AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Acute myocarditis carries a variable prognosis. We evaluated the morbidity and mortality rates in patients with acute myocarditis and admission electrocardiographic predictors of outcome.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Patients admitted to a tertiary hospital with a clinical diagnosis of acute myocarditis were evaluated.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: 193 patients were included. Median follow-up was 5.7 years; 82% were males, median age of 30 years (21-39). The most common clinical presentations were chest pain (77%) and fever (53%). The 30-day survival rate was 98.9%. Overall survival during follow-up was 94.3%. The most common abnormalities observed on electrocardiogram were T wave changes (36%) and ST segment changes (32%). Less frequent changes included abnormal T wave axis (>105° or < -15°, 16%), abnormal QRS axis (12%), QTc > 460 (11%) and QRS interval ≥ 120 ms (5%). Wide QRS-T angle (≥100(o)) was demonstrated in 13% of the patients and was associated with an increased mortality rate compared to patients with a narrow QRS-T angle (20% vs. 4%; p=0.007). The rate of heart failure among patients with a wide QRS-T angle was significantly higher (36% vs. 10%; p=0.001). Cox regression analysis demonstrated that a wide QRS-T angle (≥100(o)) was a significant independent predictor of heart failure (HR 3.20, 95% CI 1.35-7.59, P<0.01) and of the combined endpoint of death or heart failure (HR 2.56, 95% CI 1.14-5.75, P<0.05).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: QRS-T angle is a predictor of increased morbidity and mortality in acute myocarditis.
